name: Voice Input
description: Use a global shortcut to type what you say into any app. Speech is recognized on this computer or by a server you choose.
about: Use a global shortcut to type what you say into whichever app you are using. On this computer you can choose Qwen3-ASR 1.7B or 0.6B. When you recognize speech on this computer, you download the selected model and run it with the included llama.cpp. You can instead send your speech to any OpenAI-compatible server you choose, such as OpenAI or one on your network. You can choose the language you speak and leave out filler words; on this computer Gode’s vocabulary also corrects names the model spells out. A model can also tidy up what you say and follow your corrections, on this computer with Qwen3.5 4B or 2B or through your own model service, such as DeepSeek. Dictation history stays on this computer. Your vocabulary, including words you add and terms learned from dictations, can sync to your other computers. When you use a server, the vocabulary is also sent to it to help recognition. When you tidy up through your own model service, what you say and your vocabulary are sent to it.

removeFillers.title: Remove Filler Words
polish.title: Tidy Up with a Model
polish.description: A model also works out what you meant when you change your mind while speaking: it leaves out what you take back, from a single word to everything before it, keeps the rest, and leaves out words said twice or that carry no meaning. It may change your wording, and the text takes a moment longer to appear.
polishModel.title: Tidy-Up Model
polishModel.description: Qwen3.5 4B understands corrections best (2.7 GB download). Qwen3.5 2B is faster and needs less memory and disk space (1.3 GB download). With your own model service, such as DeepSeek, what you say is sent there to be tidied up.
polishServerURL.title: Service Address

polishServerModel.description: The model's name at that service, such as deepseek-chat.
removeFillers.description: Leaves out sounds such as “um” and “uh” said while thinking, and words said several times in a row by accident.
